verdict.line: You lose if Nasus free-farms Siphoning Strike stacks past level 9 unchallenged; you win if you force trades and dives before his Q stacks and Fury of the Sands come online.

brief.thesis: Nasus is a scaling matchup entirely gated by Siphoning Strike (Q) last-hits — every stack he gets uncontested is permanent power you can never claw back. Volibear's early trade tools (Q stun, W on-hit, E zone control) are strongest exactly when Nasus is weakest, levels 1-5, so this is a lane where you must actively deny farm rather than just outscale passively. OP.GG's own read confirms it: contest with E, don't let him stack, dive at 6.

theirWindow.when: you sit back and let him farm freely
theirWindow.what: Every uncontested Siphoning Strike kill adds permanent bonus damage to his Q, and every minute he's left alone he closes the gap on your early lane lead. Passivity here is what loses the matchup, not a single bad trade.

yourWindow.when: levels 1-5, before his Wither (W) hits 11s cooldown
yourWindow.what: Trade in on cooldown with Q (12/11.5/11/10.5/10s) into W (5s, re-castable on the same target for bonus damage and healing) — he has no stun and his only peel is a slow on a 15/14/13/12/11s cooldown. Use E (Sky Splitter, 16s cooldown, 1200 range) to zone him off the minion he needs to land Q on.

start.item: Doran's Ring + Health Potion + Health Potion
start.why: Taken in 75.5% of games at 48.6% win rate — the sustain from two potions lets you keep shoving trades on Nasus without backing off to heal.

boots.why: Most-picked boots at 31.4% pick rate (44.2% win) — Nasus's autos and Spirit Fire DoT are physical, and the reduced auto damage directly undercuts his all-in once he's stacked.

core.why: First item in the top build path (60% win rate, 11.6% pick) — ramps your trading power fastest in the window where Nasus is weakest
Second in the same core path — stacks attack speed into Relentless Storm procs for repeated W resets
Closes out the top core path with 60% win rate — sustain scales your W heal for extended trades as Nasus's Wither slows get longer

situational.when: he's stacked Siphoning Strike heavily and leans on lifesteal-fueled all-ins
his Wither slow and team CC are the bigger problem instead of raw auto damage
you're ahead and want to skirmish and wave-clear faster to keep denying his stacks

runes.keystoneWhy: Taken in the top rune page (44.6% win, 30.5% pick) — ramping attack speed rewards the repeated-trade, stand-and-fight pattern you need to deny his Q stacks rather than one burst window.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is both the most-picked (80.2%) and highest win-rate (48%) combo — Ignite punishes his low early lifesteal from Soul Eater and secures the all-in kills that deny stacks.

playing.title: Punish before level 6 hard
playing.detail: Nasus has no stun and a long-cooldown slow (Wither, 15s at rank 1) — use Q's stun into W on cooldown every time he goes for a Siphoning Strike last hit.

playing.title: Zone the cannon minion with E
playing.detail: Sky Splitter (16s cooldown, 1200 range) lets you threaten the exact minion he needs for a guaranteed Siphoning Strike kill without walking into his Q range (255).

playing.title: Dive at 6, not before
playing.detail: Stormbringer disables nearby towers temporarily on landing — use this window to force a kill under turret before his Fury of the Sands (120s cooldown) is online to bail him out.

playing.title: Track his Wither cooldown
playing.detail: At 15/14/13/12/11s cooldown by rank, if Wither is down he has zero kiting tools against your Q stun — that's your green light to all-in.

playing.title: Don't facetank Spirit Fire
playing.detail: Standing in Spirit Fire (650 range) strips your armor over time, which compounds badly against his scaling auto damage — step out and re-engage with Q instead of trading inside it.

playing.title: Respect the stack snowball
playing.detail: Once he's past roughly 100+ Siphoning Strike stacks his trades even out per the mid-game power curve — your real edge closes after level 9, so bank kills before then.

playing.title: W double-cast for sustain
playing.detail: Frenzied Maul's second cast on a marked target heals you — use this specifically in extended trades to outlast his Soul Eater lifesteal.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live OP.GG games on patch 16.19.1; the mechanical reasoning and timing windows are my own read of the ability kits.

stats.opponentTip: Do not let Nasus grow during early game by applying pressure to win lane control. Use [E] to contest lane and after reaching level 6 dive under turret.
